t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on deep navy. Light-weight sans-serif headline top left. A large extreme macro close-up of a glossy curving pipe weld seam in cold silver-blue monochrome, shallow depth of field, sweeps vertically through the centre-right. Over it, a dotted steel-blue timeline rises from left to upper right with glowing circular nodes, each stage of <CONTENT> labelled with a slash number, a monospace quoted duration and short bullets. The final figure sits in a box with corner brackets. Registration crosshair, mono footer caption.
signature_idea: A rising timeline of hold points is drawn over a macro weld, so schedule and craftsmanship read in one image.
strengths: rising timeline with hold points is a clear model for stage durations
light headline, mono durations and navy palette are on-brand
boxed 12-month PQ figure gives a strong anchor
weaknesses: text overlaps the busy macro image and becomes hard to read
stages are duplicated and mislabelled (two FAT, two Fabrication), clutter
photo-real glossy macro looks like stainless or chrome, not polypropylene
cinematic blur is moodier than calm, precise brand
timeline order zigzags rather than reading left to right cleanly
brand_fit_why: Navy, light headline, mono figures and hairline overlays fit, but the dark photo-real macro and overlapping labels lose the calm, legible, line-art precision.
